Comparing current Neighbour with the Farmer finds three remaining opaque pixels at frame 4 (22,42) #f6ddc4, (22,43) #5c4e92 and frame 14 (24,43) #f6ddc4. Their intent is unverified; they are recorded for art review, and no shipped PNG was changed. The pipeline alpha fix remains separate on card w6ef64f2e6dd. prior_results.result:
I hit a hard wall: this session's shell only allows trivial filesystem checks (`ls`, `file`) — every command that actually executes logic (`python3`, `godot`, even `awk`) is blocked pending an approval that isn't available in an unattended run. I can't decode PNG pixel data by hand, so I can't produce the per-sheet/frame/pixel-count/coordinate table you asked for from this session.

What I did instead: wrote the actual scan script, ready to run —
`/tmp/claude-1000/-home-daniel-dev-tiny-farm-godot/59440ba9-4637-4601-a2df-fe1bf81986b5/scratchpad/scan_white_edges.py`

It does exactly what you specified: for each sheet in `assets/sprites/generated/*.png`, flood-fills from the sheet's four edges across pixels that are either transparent or opaque near-white (R,G,B ≥ 245, alpha ≥ 250), so it only flags near-white pixels that are actually connected to the outside — not white paint that's part of a drawn shape. It reports file, per-frame pixel counts, and (x,y) coordinates local to each frame. I aimed it at `neighbour.png` and the frame-square assumption specifically so frames 4 and 14 fall out naturally, but I haven't been able to execute it, so I can't confirm the 53-vs-56 gap you described — that's still unverified.

What blocks it: no approved way to run an interpreter in this session. What it needs: one normal engineering session (interactive, or a build worktree with Bash execution approved) to run `python3 scan_white_edges.py` — it needs Pillow, which may need `pip install pillow` first — and capture the printed report.

What this implies: the inventory step is stalled on a tooling gap, not on the defect itself — the defect (five of seven hand edits hitting the same thing) is credible enough that the real fix is still the pipeline's alpha step, which is already queued as its own item. This scan is diagnostic evidence for that fix, not a separate fix in itself.
